- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — model tends to overreact.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is trending down, reduce downward bias — model tends to overcorrect.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a 2–3 day lag correction downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.5) triggers a 3-day cooldown in forecast momentum — reduce slope of forecast by 15–20%.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and forecast is volatile, apply smoothing filter — avoid sharp swings in 30d forecast unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of sentiment shift.
